items.description: 16 elective units to be chosen from the following courses, with at least 4 units from area A, and at least 8 units from area B

narrative:
Students will be admitted to full Film and Media Studies major status only after they complete Film and Media Studies 46, 70, and 96 with no grade below C.
Students planning to major in Film and Media Studies are strongly encouraged to declare Pre-Film and Media Studies as early as possible. Students are recommended to complete both the pre-major and preparation for the major during the first or second year of study. Admission to the pre-major does not guarantee admission to the Film and Media Studies major. Students must complete the pre-major before attempting enrolling in Core Upper-Division Major Requirements (the FAMST 101 History Series and FAMST 192 Theory Series), which include the 101 History series and the 192 Theory series.

MAJOR REGULATIONSPREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Not allowed for major courses (prep or UD major), including courses applied to the major from other departments.
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS With the approval of each department chairperson, up to a total of 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

nodes.title: Visual Literacy
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: An introductory survey of visual culture, encompassing art and film theory and practice, digital technologies, television, advertising and print media, with a special focus on current interdisciplinary methodologies.

nodes.title: The Intersections of Art and Life
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Explores art in relation to time-based activity and integration with everyday life. Conceptual introduction to authorship, authenticity, and narrative through exercises and examples of performance, video, film, book, arts, sound, digital media, and interactive/chance derived work.

nodes.title: Introduction to Contemporary Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Art 1A or Upper Division
nodes.description: A basic beginning survey of contemporary art, film and media theory, focusing specifically on: realism, formalism, semiotics, phenomenology, psychoanalysis, feminism, Marxism, gender/queer studies, poststructuralism, post-colonial theory and broader issues of authorship, narratology, postmodernism, and multiculturalism.

nodes.title: Introduction to Architecture and Environment
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Architecture is an act of place-making through which humans have constructed their relation with nature. Introduces the history of these strategies of place-making, interpretative concepts, and discipline-specific terminology in order to develop a critical understanding of the relationship between nature and built form.

nodes.title: Introduction to Museum Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Designed to introduce students to various aspects of Museum Studies- historical, theoretical, and practical- by examining a range of issues and topics with which the field is engaged.

nodes.title: Art Survey II: Renaissance-Baroque Art
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Renaissance and baroque art in Northern and Southern Europe.

nodes.title: Art Survey III: Modern-Contemporary Art
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Introduction to the modern era of Western art history, focusing on European and American histories. It begins reviewing the 18th-century European Enlightenment: scientific inquiry and new forms of representation are the models for the course. Proceeding through the 19th-century histories of colonization and land grabs, and then move to the 20th-century, focusing on the rise of urbanism, migration, and new developments in abstract art; additional focus on ethnicity, race, sexuality and gender across the Arts & Crafts Movement, and the rise of internationalism and global art histories in the 21st-century, ending the course by examining the present time period.

nodes.title: Survey: History of Art in China
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Chronological and thematic overview of the major traditions of Chinese art, Neolithic to modern, including ceramics and bronzes, Buddhist visual culture, paintings, calligraphy, garden design and imperial architecture, with an emphasis on historical context, regional diversity, and intercultural encounters.

nodes.title: WORLD CULTURES AND CURRENTS
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Explores how cultural encounters shaped the history of globalization from antiquity to the present by evaluating the long history of Africa-Europe encounters as revealed through visual culture. Uses the landmark publication The Image of the Black in Western Art as a principal framework for exploring the long history of African presence in Europe from classical antiquity to the present. Through analysis of paintings, sculpture, manuscripts, mosaics, prints, decorative arts, and photography, students examine how images of Africans in Western art illuminate commercial exchange, religious devotion, diplomacy, military alliances, migration, artistic patronage, and cultural interaction across continents.

nodes.title: Survey: Architecture and Planning
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: A selective and chronological survey of architecture and urban design in social and historical context. Individual buildings and urban plans from the past to the present will be used as examples.

nodes.title: Survey: History of Photography
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: A critical survey of nineteenth and twentieth century photography as an art form.

nodes.title: Survey: Arts of the Ancient Americas
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: An introduction to select art traditions from Mesoamerica to Andean South America. Examines architecture, ceramics, sculpture, painting and other classes of material culture for their meaning and function within sociopolitical, religious, and economic contexts.

nodes.title: The Arts of the Iberian World, 1492-1700
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: This survey course offers an overview of the varied artistic cultures developed under the Spanish Empire during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, covering, besides the Iberian Peninsula, different parts of Europe and North and West Africa, the Spanish Americas, and a number of transpacific territories. In addition to exposing students to an astoundingly rich set of materials, it introduces them to key theoretical themes, such as Indigenous agency, borderlands and frontier territories, religious intolerance and coercion, cross-cultural exchange, resistance, racialization, and revisions of the center/periphery and hybridity/mestizaje models.

nodes.title: Survey: Contemporary Architecture
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Global survey of architectural production in the twenty-first century. Emphasis on form and technology, as well as economic, sociopolitical context. Explores built form at a variety of scales (buildings, cities, virtual spaces), as well as the concept of a contemporary.

nodes.title: Survey: Islamic Art and Architecture
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: A survey of Islamic art and architecture.

nodes.title: Playful Spaces: A Cultural History of Games
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: This course introduces students to the history of games. It is organized chronologically as a global survey. We study games and the social, political, and economic conditions that support them, as well as the interface between the human player and the imagined world of the game. Taking as its premise that games are artifacts of culture, this course focuses on the visual and spatial practice of games in social context.

nodes.title: Survey: Eccentric Images
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.prereq_text: No prerequisites for the course.
nodes.description: This course examines the history of art through some of its strangest images, including spatial illusions, chance images, hidden faces and monsters, reversible images, caricatures and others. Primarily focused on the early modern period (1400-1750), we also consider similar experiments from other cultures.

nodes.title: Introduction to Asian American History, 1850-Present
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: Historical survey of Asian Americans in the United States from 1850 to the present. Topics include: Immigration patterns, settlement and employment, race and gender relations, community development, and transnational connections.

nodes.title: American Migration Since 1965: Asians and others in the United States
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: An examination of central themes in immigration law and policy, especially after the Immigration Act of 1965. The class focuses on Asian immigrants, but covers immigration trends comparatively. Topics include economic integration, interracial conflict, subsequent immigration reforms and their consequences.

nodes.title: Introduction to Asian American Popular Culture
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: A historical survey of how Asians and Asian Americans have been represented in American popular culture, with an analytical focus on the social and symbolic contents of examples in journalism, literature, theater, and television.

nodes.title: Introduction to Asian American Literature
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.description: Selected major themes in literary texts from Asian American communities, including Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Southeast Asian Americans: dislocation/relocation; finding/inventing a usable past; poetics/politics in language; identities/ethnicities.

nodes.title: Asian American Film, Television, and Digital Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or higher.
nodes.description: Formal, historical, and cultural issues in the study of Asian American film, television, and digital media practices in independent, Hollywood, and transnational contexts. The role of cinema and visual technology in the understanding of Asian Americans in modern and contemporary culture.

nodes.title: Introduction to African-American Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: Explores historical and current social conditions of Black people in the United States. Topics include the following: origins of Black Studies; chattel slavery and resistance; Reconstruction; Jim Crow segregation; Harlem Renaissance; Black Nationalism; structural racism and anti-Blackness; Civil Rights and Black Power Movements; racial wealth gap; critical race theory and Neo-liberalism; carcerality and the prison industrial complex; white privilege and rage; and the intersection of race, gender, class, and sexuality in shaping Black identity and life chances. As a 5 unit course, BLST 1 is reading and writing intensive, with a focus on developing research skills through a Black Studies lens.

nodes.title: Introduction to African Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: A survey of the subject matter, themes, and methods of African Studies. While briefly surveying the prehistory and early states of Africa, the course focuses on the culture and society of the colonial and independence eras.

nodes.title: Introduction to Caribbean Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: A survey of the culture and society of the Caribbean. After surveying Amerindian communities and examining the impact of the Atlantic slave trade, focus will be on slavery, emancipation, African and Creole cultures,and the issues accompanying an independent nationhood status.

nodes.title: The History of Jazz
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: A survey of the historical origins and development of jazz, beginning with the West African heritage and the African-American folk tradition, and examining the social and cultural context of this twentieth-century music.

nodes.title: Introduction to African-American Literature (Part 1)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.description: African-American literature from colonial times through the Harlem Renaissance.

nodes.title: Black Arts Expressions
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: A comparative examination of the traditions of African American music, literature, dance, folklore, cinema, the visual arts, and musical theatre. No prior musical background is required, though some musicological concepts and nomenclature are employed.

nodes.title: Mass Media, Blackness and the Politics of Representation
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: The development of Black stereotypes. Studying literature, comic books, comic strips, cartoons, music, theater, cinema, broadcasting, and television, students analyze the mythical imageries which have created stereotypes.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments

nodes.title: African Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Critical perspectives on African cinema from its inception to the present. Production contexts, aesthetic/narrative strategies, ideological/ representational concerns are examined along with issues of authorship, culture, gender, identity, post-coloniality, etc.

nodes.title: Framing Blackness: African-Americans in the American Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: An examination of the representation of African-Americans in the Hollywood feature film from 1915 to the present. The course explores the relationship between screen icons and the racial attitudes held by Black and White Americans.

nodes.title: Africa in Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Explores, with examples from the dominant cinema industry, the relationship between ideology and representation, especially how Africa functions as a site of complex and conflicting meanings under the Hollywoodian gaze.

nodes.title: Contemporary Black Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: The course explores the new directions in African-American cinema with emphasis on the directors, the aesthetics and the social content of contemporary Black film. The problems of production, distribution, and exhibition will be examined.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

nodes.title: Chicano/a Film Studies
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Study of Chicano/a cinema to view film as an art form and projection of the filmmaker. Techniques, messages, and ideology stressed as instruments which propose film truth within the context of Chicano/a experience.

nodes.title: Decolonial CyberCinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 185L; upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Cybercinema is one of the most recent and innovative technologies for representing reality. What are its aesthetic forms, and how do they work to de-colonize the imagination under postcolonial conditions? Can we identify a specific "Chicana/o" criticism or aesthetics?

nodes.title: Decolonial Cyber Cinema Lab
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Chicano Studies 185; upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Mandatory Laboratory for CHST 185.

nodes.title: Greek Mythology
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.description: Introduction to the principal myths of ancient Greece and the ways in which these myths have been understood. Format and readings vary.

nodes.title: History and Appreciation of Dance
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Introduction to history and appreciation of dance. Explores dance from a wide cross-cultural perspective of cultural mutuality and diversity, established traditions, and the power of dance to bring about social change, activism and justice.

nodes.title: Introduction to Literary Study
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2.
nodes.description: Acquaints students with purposes and tools of literary interpretation. Introduces techniques and vocabulary of analytic discussion and critical writing. Some emphasis on poetry with attention also to drama, essay, and the novel.

nodes.title: Decoding Digital Literature (Critical Code Studies)
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10.
nodes.description: A cornerstone of criticism and interpretation is the question of meaning in text, whether a novel, poem, or play... or indeed, in any cultural text, whether an advertisment, campaign speech, or news article, et cetera. This course explores how we can apply this search for meaning and this process of interpretation to computers, software, and code. What is the plain, subtle, or hidden meanings in the source code of a digital story or a video game? For that matter, what about in the code of a computer virus, a space shuttle, or a predictive policing algorithm? What are the narratives, what are the poetics, what are the values and ethics and assumptions?

nodes.title: Film, Representation, and the Environment
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Introduces students to a series of films representing a range of environmental issues, ideas, and interventions. Topics include energy, water, agriculture, biodiversity, and climate change as well as the ecological impacts of media production and consumption. Special attention is paid to the ways in which film and media affect our imaginations of the world around us and impact our thoughts and actions toward human and non-human environments. Students work collaboratively on creative film projects.

nodes.title: Introduction to Cinema
groups: PRE-MAJOR REQUIREMENTS
nodes.description: An introduction to the study of film as an aesthetic and social phenomenon, and to various methods of critical analysis.

nodes.title: Media Industries and AI
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: History
nodes.prereq_text: No prerequisites.
nodes.description: A focus on the impact of Artificial Intelligence on all aspects of the Media Industries, from sports and social media to video games, animation, television, film, and talent representation. We will host a wide range of industry guests and visiting scholars each week to address vital topics and transformations in (pre- and post-)production, distribution, exhibition, and marketing across numerous domains of media.

nodes.title: Media Arts: The High and the Low: From Robots to Cyborgs
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.prereq_text: No prerequisites.
nodes.description: Born as industrial artifacts, robots, androids, and cyborgs have become representations of our fears, our hopes, and our expectations of the future. This course looks at the historical representation of human-like creations, from robots to cyborgs, and discuss media technology, techno-militarization, trans-humanism and posthumanism in the context of science-fiction cinema, literature, and new media.

groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts

nodes.title: Shakespeare + Film
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.prereq_text: No prerequisites.
nodes.description: This critical studies class examines screen adaptations of Shakespeare’s plays. It does not assume any prior knowledge of film studies or Shakespeare studies but rather serves as an interdisciplinary introduction to both methods.

nodes.title: Media Culture and Thought: Critical AI
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.prereq_text: No Prerequisites.
nodes.description: This course delves into the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) from a humanities perspective. The course aims to foster a nuanced understanding of AI's entanglement with media, encouraging students to think critically about its implications. Topics include the historical context of AI/ML, ethical considerations, algorithm bias, and the impact on human experience. Practical aspects of media production related to AI will also be explored, providing a holistic view of AI in the media landscape.

nodes.title: Media Criticism
groups: PRE-MAJOR REQUIREMENTS
nodes.description: Develop the analytical tools required for a critical understanding of the interrelationship between media, culture, and society in America. Special attention given to how social structures shape media and how media products in return affect our cultural practices and patterns.

nodes.title: Advanced Film Analysis
groups: PRE-MAJOR REQUIREMENTS
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 and 70 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: A study of the basic formal dimensions of cinema: narration, space, time, and sound.

nodes.title: History of Cinema: The Silent Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 101 History Series
nodes.prereq_text: FAMST 96 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: International film history from the camera obscura to the close of the silent era in the late 1920's. Historical accounts of film as an aesthetic form, a social force, an economic institution, and a technology are considered.

nodes.title: History of Cinema: The Development of Sound Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 101 History Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: International film history from the advent of talkies through the late 1950s. Historical accounts of film as an aesthetic form, a social force, an economic institution, and a technology is considered.

nodes.title: History of Cinema: New Waves and Beyond
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 101 History Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: International film history since 1959. Historical accounts of film as an aesthetic form, a social force, an economic institution, and a technology is considered.

nodes.title: History of Electronic Media: Telegraphy to Early Television
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 101 History Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: International history of electronic media and broadcasting from telegraphy to early television. Historical accounts of telegraphy, radio, and early television as cultural forms, communications technologies, and social political and economic institutions are considered.

nodes.title: History of Electronic Media: Network TV to the Digital Era
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 101 History Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: International history of electronic media from the 1960s through the present day. Historical accounts of broadcasting, cable, satellites and digital media as cultural forms, communications technologies and social, political and economic institutions are considered.

nodes.title: Film History: International Cinema from 1989-Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 101 History Series
nodes.prereq_text: FAMST 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: International film history since 1989. Focuses on the expansion of independent and corporate-backed filmmaking around the world after the end of the Cold War as well as on a wide range of industrial, technological, cultural, and aesthetic changes.

nodes.title: Introduction to Production Technology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46; open to film and media majors only.

items.text: open to film and media majors only

nodes.description: An introduction to video production and technology, focusing on the fundamental concepts of the moving image including core aspects of shooting, lighting, sound-recording & editing. Lectures complement the hands-on labs by covering key concepts, dissecting various productions, and learning the workflow from pre to post-production.

nodes.title: Crew Production part two
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46; and, 102 or 104 or 107; and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Instruction in the basic techniques of filmmaking via the production of crew projects over two consecutive quarters. Post-production through exhibition.

nodes.title: Introduction to Animation
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A look at the techniques and history of animation with emphasis on the major styles and methods of production, including cel, direct, photo, three-dimensional and computer. Close examination of significant films combined with production of a class project.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production

nodes.title: Special Topics in Film Production
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46; and, consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Focus on one or more aspects of film production such as music, writing, directing, design, acting, independent filmmaking, cinematography, producing. Topics will vary.

nodes.title: Sound Production
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 104 or 105; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A workshop approach to explorations of sound recording, editing, and mixing. Students learn how to use professional sound editing software with an emphasis on editing for film including in 5.1-surround sound.

nodes.title: Editing
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 104 and 105; consent of the instructor.
nodes.description: A workshop approach to explorations of editing, color correction and sound mixing in project production.

nodes.title: Green Screen
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Instructor Approval Required
nodes.description: A hands-on, project-based environmental media production course. Students work in teams to leverage their collective production skills and environmental knowledge to create short films, which premiere in the Pollock Theater at the end of the quarter.

nodes.title: Lift Off
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Film and Media Studies Production
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 104 or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Lift Off is an interdepartmental collaboration with the Department of Theater & Dance. Senior BFA acting students work together with Film & Media Studies production teams to create actor reels, short Series and behind-the-scenes documentaries.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department

nodes.title: Film Programming: Magic Lantern
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46, or upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Students learn the ins and outs of organizing and executing a film series, using the IV Theater as a lab. They gain hands-on experience programming, contacting and working with distributors and filmmakers, fundraising, advertising, engaging in audience outreach, theater managing, exhibiting, researching, and reviewing.

nodes.title: Indian Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Examines the idea of national culture and the cinema of India in terms of major periods, themes, formal parameters, and institutions in relation to both national and international cultural histories.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing
nodes.description: Introduces students to Latin American theories, practices and representations about the media, analyzing from a cross-cultural and comparative perspective various cultural productions of the Spanish-speaking world that cross the domains of word, image, and sound.

nodes.title: Russian Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Introduction to the development of Soviet cinema from the early days to thepresent. A focal point will be the interaction between politics/ideology and film in Russia. Major directors such as Eisenshtein and Tarkovski will be treated extensively. Readings and lectures in English.

UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Popular Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: FAMST 46 or 70 or junior status or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: The course approaches pornography as a major instance of film and popular culture, from the pre-history and history of cinema and video to the Internet and virtual worlds. Course content augmented by guest lectures from the adult industry and academia.

nodes.title: Women and Film: Feminist Perspectives
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Survey of the major debates on questions of women and representation in contemporary film criticism. Topics to be covered include the representation of sexuality and the family in the Hollywood cinema; feminism and the avant-garde.

nodes.title: Film Noir
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Study of the conventional themes, structures, and visual motifs of the detective film. American films of the forties and fifties and contemporary American and European works will be considered.

nodes.title: Experimental Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A survey of the experimental film tracing the major stylistic and thematic trends in the diverse movements that have considered themselves outside of the commercial narrative cinema. Bunuel, Dulac, Cocteau, Leger, Deren, Brakhage, Baillie, Frampton, Snow, Rainer, and others.

nodes.title: Introduction to Environmental Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.description: Ties the acquisition of critical viewing skills for film to the practice of conceiving and writing short environmental documentaries. Students screen narrative films and documentaries, deconstruct them, and use their new proficiency to write their own documentary treatments.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department

nodes.title: Film Music
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Examines the musical score as an integral structural element of cinema. topics include the model of "silent" cinema; the theoretical basis of soundand image synchronicity; the narrative functions of film music; and contemporary development of the film score.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film, television, digital media, and the consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Critical Approaches to Animation
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar examines animated films as sites for critical intervention. Research methods integrate historical, theoretical and formal analysis, and discussions explore the ways in which the practices and aesthetics of animation actively engage their social, cultural and political contexts.

nodes.title: Artificial Intelligence and Media Industries
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: In this seminar, students will read and discuss current research articles and writings related to AI and the media industries. The course will consider AI tools and systems in relation to media production, distribution, and exhibition. Topics addressed include: ownership and capacities of AI tools and systems; changing work roles and labor relations; authorship, creativity, and copyright issues; AI-related modes of storytelling and aesthetics; impacts of AI on streaming and distribution; and infrastructural requirements of AI in the media industries.

nodes.title: Humane Cinema: Media and Animal Studies
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: From Eadweard Muybridge’s equine motion photography experiments to lions and tigers and bears (oh my), to an internet made of cats, animals and media have always been inextricably linked. This course takes a multifaceted, interdisciplinary approach to the study of onscreen beasts. How have animals been used as characters, as actors, as metaphors? What are the ethics of putting real animals onscreen? What do stories about animals tell us about ourselves? We will consider fictional and nonfictional modes of storytelling, historical and contemporary works, real and computer-generated creatures in our global cinematic safari. Screenings may include Nope, Jaws, Princess Mononoke, Grizzly Man, and EO.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Buster Keaton
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Buster Keaton's silent comedies in depth. Topics include: the history of comic performance styles, narrative and non-narrative comic film forms, the imagery and themes of modernity in American art and culture, and pragmatism as an aesthetic and philosophical stance.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Theories of Comedy
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar explores historical developments in screen comedy through the lens of various explanations for the human phenomena of comedy and laughter, with attention to questions of social and political context and changing processes of technological mediation.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.

nodes.title: Disaster Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar examines contemporary visualizations of disaster, asking how we process and respond to these images. Using large-budget films, independent films, educational films, TV shows, broadcast coverage, and experimental cinema, we will explore both the imagination of destruction as well as the use of media to document and shape narratives about existing disasters. Through these two lines of inquiry, we will explore both disasters of immediacy (“natural” disasters like floods and earthquakes, or man-made disasters like oil spills and nuclear meltdowns) and long-term disasters such as epidemics and climate catastrophe. We will also examine the importance of both disaster and subsequent relief efforts to national and imperial projects.

nodes.title: Essay Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: In this hybrid theory/practice seminar, we analyze the category of films referred to as essay films. Described as resisting classification, interrogating boundaries between fact and fiction, and transgressing dominant ways of seeing and thinking, essay films draw from and subvert a range of established practices, including nonfiction, narrative, and avant-garde cinema. What is the history of essayistic filmmaking? What does the essayistic mode offer filmmakers and scholars today? Through readings, screenings, student-led presentations, and exercises, students will gain both a conceptual foundation and hands-on experience with the essay film. The course culminates in a final independent project.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Fan Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This course allows students to closely examine and analyze the communities that arise around the shared enjoyment of an aspect of popular culture.

nodes.title: The Future of Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar takes a critical-industrial approach to analyzing 21st century digital media culture. We survey ongoing developments related to social media, streaming media, advertising, business models, and content development, among other topics, throughout the quarter. We also look at the various stakeholders ranging from Hollywood studios, Big Tech corporations, music and gaming companies, and YOU - the user - in order to understand the forces controlling, directing, creating, obstructing, and/or unleashing whatever is on the horizon for medias future.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis Global Cinema Going
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Explores prevailing themes in contemporary and historical film exhibition in a variety of global contexts. Readings include scholarly work and popular sources to assist students in reflecting on the research process and preparing a high-quality paper.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Global Genres
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Discusses the transnational iterations of diverse genrescomedy, melodrama, science fiction, action cinema, and horror to situate genres as expressive forms that respond to popular anxieties around change, movement, and dislocation engendered by the geopolitical flux.

nodes.title: Gender, Romance, and Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Explores how films about romantic love shape, reinforce, or challenge cultural norms of gender and sexuality. Focusing on romantic comedies, melodramas, and global reworkings of these genres, the course traces how constructions and critiques of romance appear in cinema from classical Hollywood to the present. Readings from feminist film theory, queer theory, and sociology guide discussions on spectatorship, heteronormativity, gender performativity, race and masculinity, and more.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Latin American Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Study of the central issues in contemporary Latin American cinema from 1990 to the present with an emphasis on aesthetics, social and political cultures, and global networks.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Marxist Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Is Marx still useful in addressing social inequalities still prevalent in our times? This course aims to answer this question by examining a series of political films that attempt to challenge the logic of modern capitalism from a Marxist perspective.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Media and Violence
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar examines several of the issues related to representations of and discourses about violence in film and media. We begin with a consideration of the precursors to and emergence and consolidation of the so-called "ultraviolent" aesthetic (in the mid-to-late 1960s), then we consider a few of the film genres whose most prominent conventions include representations of violence (such as the gangster, horror, war, and boxing genres). In addition, the seminar includes a comparative approach to the issue of violent representations in film and media (especially television) by surveying the terms and themes that characterize both social scientific and humanities discourses.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Oil Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar examines how our dependency on oil shapes modern ways of seeing and being. The course traces the media worlds of oil, from the origins of documentary film to contemporary contemplations of a world after oil.

nodes.title: Occult and Psychedelic Horror
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Focuses on the occult and/or psychedelic dimensions of horror films and popular culture. Critical, historical, and theoretical approaches to fear, disgust, the monster, the supernatural, delirium, esotericism, limit experiences, “good” and “bad trips.”

nodes.title: Pakistani Cinema: Exploring the Nation through Cinema from 1947-Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: What do you think when you think of “Pakistan?” What feelings does it engender? What visions does it (re)create? What about “Pakistan” and “cinema?” This course examines the idea of a national culture and the cinema of Pakistan in terms of major periods, themes, formal parameters, and institutions in relation to both national and international cultural histories. In choosing Pakistan and its cinema history which correlates with a complex political history of constantly changing regimes as our locale, we will both problematize and work through the concept of a national cinema culture through a burgeoning subfield of film studies, Pakistani cinema.

nodes.title: Russian War Films, 1911Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Examines the genre of war films in Russian and Soviet cinema from the pre-revolutionary era to the present. Together, we explore films on Russian military conflicts from World War I to the ongoing war in Ukraine. Following the evolution of a wide range of cinematic styles through the historic peripeteia of Russian imperialist, Soviet, and post-Soviet societies, we explore how movies have shaped the countrys popular historical narratives. In addition to viewing and discussing a feature-length film each week, we discuss short readings on the history of Russian cinema. Students also write weekly posts on the viewing assignments, which will go towards the creation of a collective zine.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film and its consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics of film, television and digital media.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Screendance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This course asks students to consider dance-like rhythmic movement to be integral to its representation as screen media. In addition to written assignments, students are asked to produce a short video production drawing on the reading and weekly screenings.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis:Adaptation Studies: Screening Shakespeare
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar investigates how to study screen adaptations, focusing on Shakespeare, arguably the most adapted author. Film and TV-focused topics covered include intertextuality, critical race theory (#ShakeRace), and queer theory. Screenings may include: Haider, Romeo + Juliet, Game of Thrones.

nodes.title: The Selfie from Caravaggio to the Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: The digital “selfie" is ubiquitous. But what constitutes the lure of reproducing one’s image through technical media in the first place? This course examines histories and theories of self-imaging media, tracing how widespread concepts of selfhood have shifted over time alongside––and in relation to––the development of specific media technologies: from paintings to daguerreotypes, snapshots, cinema, video, and digital media. By analyzing broad tends and “case studies” of specific artists, filmmakers, and theorists; we will ultimately consider the historical context, and develop the conceptual skills, needed to survey and scrutinize ethical problems and potentials posed by selfies in the present.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Youth Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This seminar examines the origins and development of the American media's many preoccupations with youth, including as on-screen protagonists and a key demographic off-screen. Issues explored include: the terms and meanings of "youth media" and "youth culture"; themes associated with youth; and the ways producers have sought to attract youth.

nodes.title: Basic Screenwriting
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A study of the creativity and the technique of screenwriting for the conventional narrative film and for TV. Students will be required to complete writing exercises, a treatment, and master scenes of a full-lengthproject.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department

nodes.title: Advanced Screenwriting
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 188A.
nodes.description: A course intended for students who have successfully completed Film Studies188A and have a full-length screenplay in process which they want to complete.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department

nodes.title: Musical Theatre
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: An introduction to the unique techniques and challenges of writing for musical theatre, focusing on the collaborative art of telling a story through music, lyrics, script (the “book”) and dance. A historical overview of musical theater from early operetta to contemporary Broadway and West End hits, will inform our exploration of both the “show” and the “business.” Students will learn foundational vocabulary, analyze how songs advance character and plot, and develop scenes and songs in weekly, hands-on exercises, culminating in a workshop presentation of original works-in-progress.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department

nodes.title: Short Form Comedy
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A fast-paced, writing-intensive dive into the world of sketch-writing, digital shorts, monologues, and stand-up comedy. We explore the foundational principals of scene-structure, joke-structure, and comedic voice through analysis of classic and contemporary examples, with an emphasis on developing your own unique point-of-view. Through in-class collaboration and a supportive “room-writing” environment, writers practice pitching, punching-up, producing, and performing individual, team, and group-generated material on a professional deadline, culminating in a performance/portfolio of written work, as well as tools to take a funny idea from concept to completion.

nodes.title: Storytelling for the Screen
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor, writing sample, upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Part one of a two-part program. Aimed at students who already have basic screenwriting strengths, and are in the intermediate-to-advanced skill range. While focus will depend on the writer-in-residence, the course will include sessions in plot and structure, character and dialogue, tension and conflict, tone and symbolism, and revision strategies.

nodes.title: Writing for Television
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Introduction to fundamentals of writing for television including: the situation comedy, the hour-long drama, the MOW, the miniseries, and children's programming. Investigation of the practical and creative tools necessary for programming. Investigation of the practical and creative tools necessary for navigating successful television scripts.

nodes.title: The Writers Room
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: FAMST 188A; Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A writing-intensive practicum in creative collaboration. Working together, students will develop skills of improvisation, team-ideation, and room-writing to harness the power of diverse perspectives as we conceptualize, develop, and generate scripted material.

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: Topics vary each year and may include such problems as the relation of film and other media to globalization, feminist aesthetics, critical race theories, technologies, algorithms, and the writings of key authors.

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Algorithms and Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: In this seminar, students take a critical design approach to analyze various algorithms (i.e., Search, PageRank), their relationship with their structured data (i.e., tweets), and their impact on contemporary infrastructures and social flows.

nodes.title: Alternative Media Futures
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: Topics vary each year and may include such problems as the relation of film and other media to structuralism, semiotics, metaphor/metonymy, point of view, and the writings of Burch, Barthes, Metz, Heath, Bordwell, Willemen, Wollen.

nodes.title: Cozy Games
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: Provides an opportunity to probe deeply into the genre of “cozy” games, which came to prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic with games like Animal Crossing: New Horizons (2020). We consider not only how gentle, wholesome, and domestic games predated the “cozy” label, but also how the moniker “cozy” predates cozy games (for instance, in cozy mysteries). In addition to questioning the typical gender coding of these games and their players, we will read and play extensively in order to think about the genre’s contested boundaries and why its classic themes of comfort, domesticity, and interpersonal relations often dovetail with (implied) violence, nature and the outdoors, and even death.

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: FemTech Lab
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: FemTech Lab is a theory/practice seminar on feminism, cyberfeminism, and feminist theories of technology. We engage the political potency of feminist media practicethe use of installations, performance, public engagements, and web-based platforms appealing for change or hacking systemic bias.

nodes.title: Invisible Labors: The Past, Present, and Future of Media Technology and Work
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: Explores how media and communications technologies, ranging from the telegraph and early computers to social media platforms and artificial intelligence, have shaped the politics of work and workplace control. Introduces students to theories of race, gender, and work, as well as literature from science and technology studies, the history of technology, and labor studies.

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Japanese American Internment Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: Explores the role of visual and print media in the WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans through various historical and theoretical perspectives. Topics include the production and remediation of domestic wartime propaganda, race and representation, and public and private memory.

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Media and Globalization
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: This theory course explores medias constitutive role in our experiences of globalization. Topics include: accumulation of capital and forms of dispossession; borders and migration; flows and frictions; geographies of displacement; global media conglomerates and piracy; risk and securitization; resource extraction, the commons, and grassroots mobilization.

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory – Film & Media and Policing
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: This seminar investigates the relationship between police power and film and media from the late nineteenth century to the present. Students will analyze a range of media including, photography, silent cinema, American and international studio and independent features, avant-garde film, dash cam, body cam, and cell phone footage, and digital technologies that employ crime statistics and predictive policing. In addition to film and media theory, students will study theories of criminality, punishment, and abolition.

nodes.title: Sports, Media and Modernity
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: Explores the relationship between sport, media, and modernity through two critical lenses: first, how sport acts as a cultural apparatus mediating institutions, collective identities, and power structures of modern societies; second, how evolving media technologies (from print cultures to data-driven platforms) transform how sport is staged, performed, and experienced today. Thinking through the topics of colonialism, nationalism, race, gender, technology, and spectatorship, students examine how sport both expresses and structures the cultural dynamics of modern life.

nodes.title: Occult Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: In this seminar, we will contend with definitions of media and how they interface with the occult. Throughout the quarter, students will conduct archival research, learn about media archaeology, and discover occult media in its many forms, including horror films, online folklore, divination tools, Ouija boards, tabloid reports of the Satanic Panic, magic lantern shows, spiritualist and countercultural periodicals, optical toys, podcast episodes, popular music, religious technology like Scientology’s E-Meter, and more. Each student will be guided through a personalized archival research project that includes a trip to special collections at UCSB Library.

nodes.title: Race and/in AI
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: Critical work on artificial intelligence has, by now, revealed it as an intense tool of surveillance, policing, and racialization. This work has demonstrated the vastly unequal distributions of the political effects of race; however, this work has also demonstrated alternative practices, both current and speculative, with, alongside, and/or against AI. This course traces these diverse accounts of race and/in AI with the goal of answering the following three questions: What, when, and where is race in AI?

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: Sound, Media, and Society
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: Builds conceptual and analytical tools for a critical understanding of sound, media, and auditory cultures. Special attention is paid to how social and historical factors inform sound media and how sound media, in turn, inform cultural perceptions and practices.

nodes.title: Software and Society
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 46 or 70
nodes.description: If “data is the new oil”—a phrase often championed by venture capitalists, Big Tech advocates, and engineers—then software might be likened to refineries that transform raw data into commodities, video games, and social media platforms. But what exactly is software, and how does it interact with social, political, and cultural forces? This course explores these questions by tracing software's history from the mid-20th century to today’s Artificial Intelligence systems. We will examine primary and secondary sources to understand software’s role in everything from surveillance and warfare to art and finance. Our central goal will be to develop our understanding of how, as one popular commentary puts it, “software is eating the world.”

nodes.title: Topics in Contemporary Media Theory: The Wire: TV in Focus
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media Studies 96
nodes.description: Examines HBOs crime drama television series, The Wire (2002-2008). Discusses the series through critical, historical, and theoretical approaches from fields like urban studies and television studies. Students work on projects related to city media of their choice.

nodes.title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: An analysis of film and other media in relation to literary and plastic arts such as photography, architecture, and the novel. Topics vary.

nodes.title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts: Anti-War Media
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: In this seminar, we focus on global and local oppositional media and crafts practices that seek to prevent, stop, and undermine the death-making of war, offering ways to sustain life for civilians, heal the survivors, and commemorate the dead: From memoirs and photographs to zines and social media, from carpets and cooking recipes to apps and video games. By Interrogating warfare through anti-war media, we closely engage with the ethics of witnessing, limits of representation, and militarization of everyday life. Simultaneously, by studying media through anti-war frameworks we consider less-discussed aspects, kinds, and practices of media such as failure and repair, handmade and low-tech, and tactical and communal.

nodes.title: Studies in Film, Media and the Other Arts
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: An analysis of film and other media in relation to literary and plastic arts such as photography, architecture, and the novel. Topics vary.

nodes.title: Women, Work, and Gambling
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. Seminars in Theory and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This rigorous, interdisciplinary seminar examines contemporary gaming, gambling, and digital media platforms. In this course we ask: How are entertainment and work shaped by capitalism and mediated by digital platforms? Who works and plays on digital platforms? How does digital media change, distort, warp, or adapt our work lives and leisure time? Drawing from texts in feminist studies, history, sociology, critical theory, gaming and gambling studies, political economy, and film theory, students will develop a high-quality, well-argued, original final paper throughout the quarter. Students will closely engage with course texts and fellow classmates’ written work in writing workshops.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Addresses film, television and/or digital media from a variety of theoretical perspectives; topics will vary depending on instructor. Critical analytical papers will be required. Emphases have included classical, contemporary and comparative theories of film and media.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Cultural Thory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: This course introduces students to theoretical approaches and frameworks that are crucial to understanding our social and cultural contemporaneity. Topics include ideology and social determination; knowledge and power; history, memory, and trauma; postcolonial/decolonial critique; neoliberal globalization; biopolitics; risk and precarity.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Digital Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Histories and theories of digital media and their users, from early computers and networks to video games and selfies. Approaches include comparative media analysis, cultural studies, science and technology studies, software/platform studies, and environmental media critique.

nodes.title: Theories of Filmgoing and Mass Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: In our age of online streaming platforms, diminishing theatrical ticket sales, and individual media devices, one may reasonably ask: what is the value of filmgoing in a space shared with others? This course will help us consider this pressing question by engaging past and present theories of cinema’s effect on landscapes of mass culture. Beginning with film photography at the cusp of modernity, before tracing positive and negative appraisals of cinema’s ideological power, we will ultimately consider arguments for why public filmgoing should matter: insofar as collective viewership may challenge insufficient assumptions, open up newfound ethical possibilities, and incite astonishing alternatives to the status quo.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Addresses film, television and/or digital media from a variety of theoretical perspectives; topics will vary depending on instructor. Critical analytical papers will be required. Emphases have included classical, contemporary and comparative theories of film and media.

nodes.title: Genre Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Examines the study of film genres through a theoretical lens. Topics include semiotic, structuralist, psychoanalytic, and phenomenological theories of the musical, the horror film, melodrama, and the concept of genre itself.

nodes.title: Topics in Film and Media Theory: Popular Music and Youth Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: 192 Theory Series
nodes.prereq_text: Film and Media 96 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Explores the social history and cultural politics of popular music and youth culture, with an emphasis on the relations between musical meaning, technological mediation, cultural value, and social power.

nodes.title: Fairy Tale Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B. Elective courses in the department
nodes.prereq_text: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Online course that addresses a number of fairy tales & related films. It examines the ways in which tales of wonder provide a metaphoric context for human adaptation and interpretation. Fairy tales evoke themes of childhood, development, & home, as well as critical methods including structuralism and psychoanalysis. Through a focus on films, presented weekly for screening, along w/ relevant descriptive, theoretical, & literary texts, we take a critical approach to fairy tales. You will be required to respond to writing prompts related to a weekly screening, write weekly forums along w/ a midterm & final for the course. Your active participation in the course activities & attendance for the synchronous portions of the course are essential.

nodes.title: Black Women Filmmakers
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.description: An opportunity to view films (animation, documentary, experimental and narrative), examine the specifics of media production, compare the various works produced by black women, and acquire the skills necessary for media criticism.

nodes.title: Representation and Activism
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Exploration of the strategies by which social groups resist systems of oppression through readings and works from independent filmmakers.

nodes.title: Tales of Love in the Western Tradition
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2.
nodes.description: A comparative and interdisciplinary approach to the literatures and philosophies of love, desire, and sexuality in the western world, in antiquity, the Middle Ages, and the Renaissance. In English.

nodes.title: Tales of Love in the Western Tradition
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.description: A comparative and interdisciplinary approach to the literatures and philosophies of love, desire, and sexuality in the western world in the 17th and 18th centuries. In English.

nodes.title: Tales of Love in the Western Tradition
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2.
nodes.description: A comparative and interdisciplinary approach to the literatures and philosophies of love, desire, and sexuality in the western world in the 19th and 20th centuries. In English.

nodes.title: French Cinema: History and Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.description: History of French cinema from 1895-present, covering the silent period, the early classic era, the war years, and the New Wave, with a survey of the major French film theories since the 1920s. In English.

nodes.title: Dreaming Revolutions: Introduction to Marx, Nietzsche, and Freud
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.description: Introduction to the revolutionary theories of Karl Marx, Friedrich Nietzsche, and Sigmund Freud. Explorations of three authors whose writing has profoundly changed our world.

nodes.title: Critical Theory Through Anime and Manga
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: This course teaches critical theories by combining academic texts by scholars and popular culture products such as anime and manga. The topics include power, hegemony, agency, ritual, magic, hybridity, among others.

nodes.title: Japanese Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: An introductory scrutiny of major Japanese directors: Mizoguchi, Ozu, Oshima, and Kurosawa. Close attention to their film composition, choices ofsubject and character, their ideas of the cinematic, and the relationship of cinema to Japanese culture and society.

nodes.title: EMS: Approaches to University Writing for Multilingual Students
nodes.prereq_text: Open to students who have not satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement and have a Ling 12 placement or a prerequisite of Ling 3C with a grade of C or better.

nodes.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking and writing in the university. Students analyze academic discourse, develop rhetorical strategies for exposition and argument, practice examination writing, and write and revise papers. Completion of C or better meets Entry Level Writing Requirement.

nodes.title: Constructing Communities through Music: Classical and Beyond
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: Examines how music builds and sustains communities across historical contexts. Students develop critical and historical thinking using case studies from Europe and the United States to explore musical practices (classical and beyond), socio-economic contexts, and continuities between past and present.

nodes.title: World Music
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Visual or Performing Arts
nodes.description: An introductory course surveying the unity and diversity of folk, traditional, and classical music of the non-western world. Emphasis given to dance, theatre, musical instruments, and the role of music in society.

nodes.title: Religion and Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Elective courses offered from other departments
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing or instructor approval
nodes.description: An examination of religious themes and forms as they appear in significant works of modern film. The nature of man, the problem of suffering, the quest for meaning are among the topics considered.

nodes.title: Play Analysis
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Literature
nodes.description: Deep study of key concepts used in the analysis of plays in performance, including story, action, genre, liveness, and experience. Includes study of exemplary plays and performances.

nodes.title: Academic Writing
nodes.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12 with a grade of "C" or better.

items.text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement

nodes.description: A writing course focusing on developing analytical skills, synthesizing multiple sources, sustaining coherent arguments, and revising for clarity of style. Reading and writing assignments are drawn from a range of academic disciplines.

nodes.title: Academic Writing for Engineers
nodes.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12; freshmen only; open to ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering majors only.

nodes.title: Writing and the Research Process
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK.
nodes.description: A writing course addressing the analytical skills underlying the research processes of various academic and professional communities. Sections vary in topic and disciplinary emphasis.

nodes.title: Writing for the Disciplines
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 2LK or 2E; upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Analysis and practice of various forms of academic and professional writing for and in the disciplines.
